detail.body:
# Description This [PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/3658) introduced rowwise/colwise swizzling kernels targeted at narrow scale width use-cases. The scope of this PR is to - Colwise Swizzling: Enable the colwise swizzling optimized kernel(swizzle_columnwise_chunk_kernel) for both narrow scale-width and wide scale-width use-cases. And completely removes the previously existing kernel for narrow scale width kernel. The previously existing kernel for wide scale-width is retained since that is still used for grouped swizzling. Using the kernel in grouped swizzling will be a follow up PR. - Rowwise swizzling: Enable rowwise swizzling optimized kernel(swizzle_rowwise_full_width_kernel) for narrow scale-width use-cases. For wide scale-width, we fall back to our previosuly existing rowwise scaling kernel which operates on 128*128*N tile where N is vectorization's bit width. Fall back is implemented through shared memory heuristics - If scale is sufficiently narrow (smem ~= 128*padded_k <= 17KB), new kernel is better - If smem is between (17,30)KB then using the new kernel turns out to be better if the number of row tiles is between 16 and 256. - Optimized row scaling kernel is also extended to be use for NVFP4. - Apt unit tests are also added ### Blackwell Perf results

Existing transpose operations select their static fallback automatically. NVFP4 4over6 quantization, fused softmax, and normalization paths require their corresponding ``NVTE_BUILD_LEGACY_STATIC_NVFP4``, ``NVTE_BUILD_LEGACY_STATIC_FUSED_SOFTMAX``, or ``NVTE_BUILD_LEGACY_STATIC_NORM`` CMake option to have been enabled when the library was built; otherwise no static fallback is available.

-
-   :Type: ``int`` (0 or 1)

-   :Description: Swizzle MXFP8 scaling factors for GEMM with kernels that give each 128-row tile of scaling factors (row-wise) or each 128-column by 32-row block (column-wise) its own thread block, instead of batching 32 tiles in one block. This lowers the latency of swizzling the scaling factors of tensors with few tiles, such as activations.

inline_comments.body: **Input size check is lost** The generic fallback now takes `m` and `k` from the output, so its output-size check always passes. If an unchecked caller supplies a larger output buffer, the kernel reads the input using those larger dimensions. That can produce wrong scales or read beyond the input instead of reporting the previous size error. Keep the input/output size check before launching, and use the input dimensions for the input layout.

**NVFP4 padding is not tested** The new single- and multi-tensor NVFP4 tests only use shapes with no scale padding. They can pass even if the newly enabled path fails to write zeros outside the original dimensions. Add padded cases in both directions, such as `M=160, K=96`. Fill the input padding with nonzero bytes and zero only the reference padding before calling `compute_ref_swizzle`. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!

**Valid columnwise scales become zero** A batch containing one MXFP8 tensor with both scale buffers and another with only columnwise scales passes the existing checks and selects the columnwise path. But `logical_rowwise = use_rowwise_buffer` uses rowwise dimensions for the first tensor, even though the selected buffer is `columnwise_scale_inv`. For a 256×128 tensor, this sets `original_k` to 4 instead of 8. The kernel then zeros half its valid columnwise scales, giving GEMM incorrect scales. Derive the limits from the selected buffer, such as with `rowwise && use_rowwise_buffer`. ```suggestion const bool logical_rowwise = rowwise && use_rowwise_buffer; ```

This PR makes the optimized swizzle kernels the default, removes obsolete narrow-scale kernels, and adds NVFP4 coverage.
